tagline: A quiet outer Asian side district at the foot of Aydos Forest — one of Istanbul's largest forested areas, with hiking trails and a hilltop castle ruin above the city.

items.name: Aydos Ormanı
items.description: One of Istanbul's largest urban forests — a vast green escape with walking and hiking trails. Remarkably peaceful given its proximity to the city.
items.tip: The forest is best visited on weekday mornings when it's almost empty. Weekends get busy with local families.

items.name: Aydos Kalesi
items.description: A Byzantine-era hilltop castle ruin with sweeping views over Istanbul and the Marmara Sea on clear days. A rewarding hike to reach.

items.name: Orman Kenarı Çay Bahçeleri
items.description: Simple tea gardens at the edge of the forest serving çay and snacks. Rustic and very local.

tips: Aydos is best reached by car or taxi — public transport connections are limited.
Wear sturdy shoes for the castle hike; the trail is uneven and steep in places.
The hilltop view on a clear day extends to the Princes' Islands and the Marmara.
Bring water — there are no facilities inside the forest.
